result.summary: This pull request replaces string-based argument registration and lookup in ArgsManager with compile-time type-safe declarations using a new common::Setting template class. Settings specify their argument string, value type, and defaults in dedicated header files. Call sites across the repository are converted from AddArg and Get*Arg calls to Setting::Register and Setting::Get invocations via a scripted diff.
result.problem: Command-line and configuration settings are retrieved and registered using raw string keys with no compile-time checking. Typos in argument names fail silently or at runtime, types can be queried inconsistently across call sites, and default values can drift between user help text and code fallbacks.
evidence: PR description: "nothing checks that setting names are spelled correctly, or that default values (BITCOIN_PID_FILENAME) are used consistently in the help string and retrieval sites, or that settings are retrieved with consistent types (bool, int, string, path, or list)."
Implements the compile-time foundation requested in RFC issue #22978 ('ArgsManager type and range checking').
result.scope_notes: Contains a large mechanical scripted diff spanning 100 files (+3733/-1128 lines) that generates multiple *_settings.h headers and replaces callsites across the codebase. Also touches build configuration (CMakeLists.txt) and linter scripts to handle the new headers.
result.changed_since_previous: Updated includes after the scripted-diff pass to clean up unused headers in init.cpp, adapted CMake target includes for libevent and UniValue dependencies across platforms, and rebased onto recent master changes.
result.card: This PR replaces string-based argument handling in ArgsManager with compile-time type-safe declarations using a new common::Setting class. Currently, settings are looked up with unchecked string literals, meaning typos are not caught by the compiler, call sites can query conflicting types, and default values can drift between help text and retrieval fallbacks. A scripted diff migrates setting registrations and lookups across 100 files to typed Setting::Register and Setting::Get calls. This provides compile-time safety and serves as the foundation for runtime type checking and validation in #16545 and #22978.

risk.why: A typo or subtle type conversion error in a setting definition could silently alter node configuration parsing across wallet, network, RPC, or validation subsystems.
